summary_of_pdf: This document captures a pre-litigation email dispute between Key Opinion Leaders (KOL) and Akamai (along with its partner Mobile Rider). KOL alleges that Akamai improperly disclosed KOL's confidential IPv4 subnet ranges to a third-party security researcher (Hunt.io) during a DDOS/web crawling mitigation effort, claiming this violated California privacy laws and put KOL's infrastructure at risk. Akamai's Chief Privacy Officer rebuts the privacy claims, noting corporate IP subnets do not constitute personal information under California law and that the disclosure was standard procedure to effectuate a blocklist. KOL further alleges a critical technical vulnerability in Akamai's Origin IP ACL mitigation, claiming attackers can bypass it by spoofing requests through a fake Akamai property. Additionally, outside counsel for Mobile Rider (Vorys) intervenes to establish ethical boundaries pending a formal conflicts check.
attorneys_comments: KOL's assertion that corporate IPv4 subnets constitute Protected Personal Information (PII) under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) lacks statutory merit; Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140 explicitly ties personal information to consumers or households, not B2B corporate infrastructure. The evidentiary strength of KOL's statutory privacy claim is de minimis. However, KOL's technical allegation regarding Akamai's Origin IP ACL bypass—specifically the ability of a malicious actor to spoof origin server requests via a fabricated Akamai property—presents a colorable negligence, breach of contract, or breach of implied warranty claim if Akamai's infrastructure fails to properly validate Host headers or isolate tenant traffic. Procedurally, this is an escalating pre-litigation dispute. Outside counsel (David Hine of Vorys) appropriately invoked principles analogous to ABA Model Rule 1.7 to pause substantive communications pending a formal conflicts check, demonstrating sound ethical decorum in the face of a hostile unrepresented or corporate party.
recommended_next_steps: 1. For KOL: Abandon the frivolous CCPA statutory claims and pivot to a breach of contract/confidentiality framework governed by the applicable Master Services Agreement (MSA). Immediately implement origin-side Host header validation and rate-limiting to mitigate the alleged Akamai ACL bypass vulnerability. 2. For Akamai: Issue a formal litigation hold on all server logs, abuse tickets, and communications pertaining to Hunt.io and KOL's origin traffic. Conduct an urgent technical review of the alleged ACL bypass vulnerability to preempt potential gross negligence or deceptive trade practice claims. 3. For Vorys/Mobile Rider: Complete the Rule 1.7 conflicts check before resuming any advisory role, and maintain strict compartmentalization of attorney-client communications away from KOL.
